tldr: In October, papers began synthesizing training environments for agents instead of collecting human demonstrations, first for computer use and then for tool use with controllable data composition. By November the work moved to MCP tool-centric synthesis and to real-source data for productivity tasks.
whats_new: Agent-R² (Nov 5) synthesizes training data from real sources to target realistic productivity work, the fourth environment-synthesis paper in 17 days.
why_it_matters: If agent capability now scales with synthesized environments, tool and MCP coverage in training data decides how well agents handle your own tool surface, and evals built on public environments may overlap with training data.
take_for_builders: Treat these as preprints: before adopting any synthesized-environment model, rerun it on your own MCP tools and check whether its benchmark environments overlap with your eval set.

status.detail: Four arXiv papers in three weeks converge on synthesized environments as the way to scale agent training; none is independently replicated yet.

beats.headline: Computer-use agents learn from synthesized environments
Tool-use scaling laws tied to environment data composition
ToolSpace makes MCP environment synthesis tool-centric rather than data-centric
Agent-R² grounds synthesis in real-source data for productivity work

open_questions: Do any of these environment-synthesis methods report results replicated by an independent group?
Are models trained on synthesized MCP environments released with weights or evals others can run?
Does synthesized-environment training show gains on real-world productivity benchmarks, not only the authors' own?
